jobs.blender_target: hall() columns/bay; even-bay bug; missing jinzhu
jobs.prompt: Technical architectural ground plan and axonometric timber-frame diagram of a Song-dynasty Chinese palace hall, Foguang Temple East Hall type. STRICT RULES: odd number of bays only — seven bays, eight columns on the front eave line. Graduated bay widths: central mingjian widest, cijian slightly narrower, jinian / corner bays narrowest. Interior gold-columns (jinzhu) form a full inner grid, not a hollow shell. Show: (A) top-left orthographic ground plan with column dots on a modular cai-fen grid, center axis empty of columns so the main portal sits in the central bay; (B) 3/4 axonometric of the post-and-lintel cage with lan'e architrave and pupaifang plate; (C) small elevation strip showing shengqi — corner columns 2 percent taller — and cejiao inward lean 8 per mille front, 10 per mille sides. Pale linen paper background, ink-and-wash measured drawing, precise wood joinery, no people, no Chinese characters, no watermarks, no fantasy glow.

jobs.blender_target: bracket(); replace box ludou + fake ang tips
jobs.prompt: Engineering exploded axonometric of one Song-dynasty seven-puzuo column-head bracket set: qi puzuo shuang-miao shuang-xia-ang, touxinzao, as at Foguang Temple. Disassemble along vertical Z with dashed alignment stems. Bottom to top, physically accurate parts: ludou cap-block 32 fen square, 20 fen tall, ear-waist-qi 8-4-8 fen, cross mortise; two huagong cantilever arms stepping out 30 fen per tiao with juansha roll-cut undersides (keep 6 fen at tips, cut 9 fen); nidao-gong on the wall axis 6.2 doukou long; guazi-gong then man-gong then ling-gong; jiaohudou cross-slot blocks at intersections; sandou single-slot blocks at arm ends; two continuous xia'ang lever beams slicing through the cluster at 15-20 degrees, pizhu-ang bamboo-shoot beaks, inner tails anchoring under an interior purlin — NOT short decorative sticks; shuatou and liaoyanfang eaves purlin plate on top. Weathered cedar #241C18 and #6B6055, chipped cinnabar #7D3227 on ludou only. White studio background, hard product-viz lighting, orthographic-ish 35-degree axon, no text, no labels, no people.

Close-up engineering view of a Song-dynasty CORNER bracket cluster (jiaopuzuo / jiaoke) at the eave corner of a timber hall. Unique 45-degree diagonal members: jiao-huagong, jiao-ang, you-ang, and a small baoping vase block at the corner. Orthogonal wall-axis gongs meet the diagonal arms in a dense interlocking nest. Show how the corner cantilever is longer by sqrt(2) than the front tiao. Two layers of round rafters plus square flying rafters (feizi) radiating from the corner, wing-corner eave lifting gently (Tang-Song, NOT sharp Qing upturn). Underside of the eave in shadow, massive structural feel like Black Myth Wukong scanned Shanxi temples. Photogrammetry wood grain, moss at joints, no text, no people, 3/4 view from below looking up into the corner.

Longitudinal structural section (ceyang) of a Song-dynasty double-eave hip-and-gable hall (chongyan xieshan). Cut through the center bay. Roof pitch generated by Yingzao Fashi juzhe: ridge height = 1/3 of hall depth; purlin drops 1/10 then 1/20 then 1/40 of remaining height, producing a gentle polygonal catenary, NOT a late-Qing hooked corner. Upper and lower eaves clearly separated by a band of dougong. Interior: yueliang crescent beams, tuofeng camel-hump blocks, purlins (tuan) at each seam. Gable pediment (shan hua) visible in a small side inset showing the hanging gable of xieshan, not a pure four-slope wudian. Grey banwa tiles, lichen, deep overhang 0.52-0.58 of column height. Ink-wash architectural section on pale paper plus one realistic shaded render of the same cut. No Chinese text, no people, no gold fantasy roofs.

jobs.blender_target: terrace(); rectangular slabs -> true xumizuo + chishou
jobs.prompt: Measured drawing of a palace Sumeru pedestal (xumizuo) for a main hall platform. Split composition: LEFT a clean vertical cross-section of six moldings from bottom to top with Song/Qing hybrid clarity — guijiao feet, xia-fang, xia-xiao carved with drooping lotus (fulian), shuyao recessed waist with humen niches and inter-pillars, shang-xiao with upturned lotus (yanglian), shang-fang. Layer height rhythm approximately 10:8:6:8:6:9. RIGHT a 3/4 photoreal view of the real stone platform: wet grey granite #565A5C, moss #344028 in recesses, iron stains, at each corner a protruding dragon-head water spout (chishou) discharging rain into a stone trough. Central stair with an inclined carved imperial ramp slab (danbi) of coiled dragons and clouds between steps. Black Myth Wukong weathering, no text, no people.

Product-design orthographic sheet of a Northern-Song chiwei / chiwen main-ridge terminal. THREE views: side elevation, front elevation, top plan, plus one 3/4 beauty render. Form: fish-dragon hybrid swallowing the ridge beam, truncated coiled body, large wide mouth clamped on the grey tile ridge, prominent dorsal fin spine, notched scales, swirling tail fins turning inward, small wings retained from Tang chiwei. Glaze: tarnished temple gold #B88B4A with malachite verdigris #4D6D63 in recesses, cracked grey earthenware body. Scale: the ornament is huge — about 1/8 to 1/6 of roof height, Black Myth monumentality. White studio background, no Chinese characters, no extra beasts in this plate.

jobs.blender_target: door_pair() banmen studs on hall; lattice_window()
jobs.prompt: Front elevation of a Song-dynasty palace hall facade, five or seven bays. CRITICAL: the entire ground-floor front is lattice partition doors (geshan men), NOT solid studded board gates. Each door leaf has four zones: lattice heart (ge xin) with pohuizhi straight-bar or wanzi swastika lattice and aged oil paper, waist panel (tiao huan ban) with simple cloud carving, skirt board (qunban) below, multiple transom rails (matou). Columns: raw/sun-bleached cedar with peeling cinnabar #7D3227. Between columns: massive interlocking dougong under a deep eave. Only the outer compound gate elsewhere would have iron studs — not this hall. Warm 2800K interior glow through paper vs cool 7000K mist outside, Where Winds Meet rain atmosphere, wet threshold stone. Photoreal, no text, one tiny human silhouette for scale.
